name: Código de Tributos
source: Anexo 8 (catálogo 05) from the 'Catálogos' sheet of perunio-facturador/resources/reglas/reglas-validacion-cpe-2026-08-26.xlsx, which gives código, descripción, código internacional (props.taxTypeCode) and nombre (props.name): all nine here match it verbatim, including the 'IGV'/'ISC' prefixes on 1000 and 2000 and SUNAT's own spelling of 'Impuesto a la bolsa plastica'. The workbook lists a tenth, 3000 (Impuesto a la Renta, TOX, IR), used only on the liquidación de compra (Cat.01 04) for retención de renta, which this platform does not issue. It is left out because SUNAT documents no cac:TaxCategory for it, and carrying it would make props.taxCategoryId nullable for every consumer. props.taxCategoryId is the UN/ECE 5305 cac:TaxCategory/cbc:ID, per the 'Valor de Códigos cbc:ID Catálogo N° 05' tables of perunio-facturador/resources/guias/guia-xml-factura-2.1-2017-05.pdf (items 23-29): S for IGV, ISC and otros tributos, E exonerado, O inafecto, Z gratuito. G for exportación is UN/ECE's free-export code; the guía gives none. SUNAT's XSL never reads that element, so a wrong value is not rejected — which is how 9996 carried E instead of Z until v1.2.0. The códigos were first transcribed from perunio-facturador/internal/model/catalog.go (TaxScheme* var block, since moved here), the only place all nine were named together; its dead UNECEID field was not carried over. props.rate is the tributo's own statutory rate and is null wherever no such rate exists: ISC varies by sistema de cálculo, and 9996 (gratuito) declares whichever rate the underlying operación would have carried — 18.00 for gravado-gratuito, 0.00 for exonerado/inafecto gratuito — which is a Cat.07 property, not a Cat.05 one. 1000's 18.00 is the general IGV rate: MYPE restaurantes, hoteles and alojamientos in SUNAT's padrón may declare 10.5 on the line instead (OBSERV 4439 when the emisor is not in it), and every IGV line of a comprobante must declare the same rate (ERROR 3462).
